The words

Along my earthly way,
How many clouds are spread!
Darkness, with scarce one cheerful ray,
Seems gathering o'er my head.

Yet, Father, thou art love:
O hide not from my view!
But when I look, in prayer, above,
Appear in mercy through!

My pathway is not hid;
Thou knowest all my need;
And I would do as Israel did, —
Follow where thou wilt lead.

Lead me, and then my feet
Shall never, never stray;
But safely I shall reach the seat
Of happiness and day.

And O from that bright throne,
I shall look back, and see, —
The path I went, and that alone,
Was the right path for me.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum Ab and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on l, (F), on the first syllable of “Along”, as a pickup before the first full bar.
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

James Edmeston wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 521 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"Why sayest thou — my way is hid from the Lord?"”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.

Questions about Along My Earthly Way

What is the doh of Along My Earthly Way?

In this version, in F minor, doh is Ab. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Along My Earthly Way start on?

It starts on l, (F in F minor), a pickup on the first syllable of “Along” before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to l,.

Is Along My Earthly Way in the public domain?

Yes. James Edmeston died in 1867; the words were in print by 1853 and the music in 1579. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
